facts.t: The Constitution never mentions a collegium
facts.d: Articles 124 and 217 say only that the President appoints in consultation with the Chief Justice. The entire collegium system was built by the Second and Third Judges Cases in 1993 and 1998 — judicial architecture with no textual foundation.

facts.t: The Supreme Court now discloses judicial family ties
facts.d: From May 2025 collegium resolutions record whether a recommended High Court candidate is related to a serving or retired judge — a direct response to persistent allegations of dynastic appointment.

facts.t: Britain picks twelve of fifteen commissioners by open competition
facts.d: Its Judicial Appointments Commission has just three judges among fifteen members. South Africa uses a 23-member Judicial Services Commission. India remains the only major democracy where judges alone select judges.

bank.q: Which case introduced the collegium system with primacy to the Chief Justice?
bank.e: The Second Judges Case of 1993, which overruled S. P. Gupta. The Third Judges Case then expanded the collegium to a plurality of judges.

bank.q: With reference to the Third Judges Case, consider the following statements:
s: Consultation was held to mean consultation with a plurality of judges.
For Supreme Court appointments the collegium comprises the Chief Justice and four senior judges.
For High Court appointments it comprises the Chief Justice and two senior judges.
bank.e: All three are correct — the composition settled in 1998 and still in force.

bank.q: Which one of the following was NOT part of the NJAC's composition under the 99th Amendment?
o: The Chief Justice of India and two senior Supreme Court judges
Two eminent jurists nominated by the CJI, Prime Minister and Leader of the Opposition
bank.e: The Attorney General had no place in the NJAC. One of the two eminent jurists was to be from the SC/ST/OBC categories, a religious minority, or a woman.

bank.q: Match List I (provision) with List II (type of appointment):
pairs: 1. Additional High Court judges for backlog
2. Ad hoc judges of the Supreme Court
3. Ad hoc judges of a High Court, added in 1963
4. Retired judges sitting in the Supreme Court
bank.e: Article 127 for Supreme Court ad hoc judges, 128 for retired judges, 224(1) for additional High Court judges, and 224A for High Court ad hoc appointments.

bank.as: The collegium system has been criticised for opacity even after 2017.
bank.rs: Published resolutions convey the decision without the comparative assessment of candidates.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion. Resolutions went unpublished until 2017, and disclosure remains partial.

bank.q: Consider the following statements on diversity in the higher judiciary:
s: A 2023 Parliamentary Standing Committee report found around 3% Scheduled Caste representation among High Court judges appointed since 2018.
The corresponding Scheduled Tribe figure was around 1.5%.
There is a constitutional requirement of at least one woman judge in the collegium.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Including at least one woman in the collegium regardless of seniority is a recommendation, not a requirement.

bank.q: As of July 2026, High Court vacancies stood at approximately:
bank.e: 341 vacancies against a sanctioned strength of 1,122, with 781 judges working — close to 30%.

bank.q: All of the following are among the new 2025 guidelines on ad hoc judges EXCEPT:
o: Ad hoc and retired judges must not exceed 10% of High Court sanctioned strength
They may only hear criminal appeals
The High Court must have more than 20% vacancies
The disposal rate must be lower than the new filing rate
bank.e: The 20% vacancy condition from the 2021 Lok Prahari guidelines was removed in the 2025 revision.

bank.q: An additional High Court judge under Article 224(1) may serve for a maximum of:
bank.e: Two years, or until the age of sixty-two, whichever is earlier.

bank.q: With reference to reform proposals, consider the following:
s: The 214th Law Commission recommended a National Judicial Service.
A dedicated Office of Judicial Appointments within the Supreme Court has been proposed.
Eminent jurists should be appointed directly to the Supreme Court.
bank.e: All three feature among the recommendations, alongside a formal nominations process and published selection criteria.

bank.q: Arrange the following in correct chronological order:
bank.e: S. P. Gupta (1981) → the Second Judges Case (1993) → the Third Judges Case (1998) → the NJAC judgment (2015).

bank.q: In the United States, a judicial nominee is assessed before Senate confirmation by:
o: A committee of the American Bar Association
bank.e: An American Bar Association standing committee rates nominees, whose assessment then informs the Senate Judiciary Committee's review.
